title: Police Arrest Five Teenagers Across Germany for Far-Right Terror Network 'Last Defense Wave'
detail: German police conducted simultaneous early-morning raids on 13 properties across multiple German states on May 21, arresting five teenagers aged 14-18 on suspicion of membership in a far-right domestic terror organization calling itself 'Die Letzte Verteidigungswelle' (The Last Defense Wave). The group allegedly planned and carried out violent attacks targeting migrants and political opponents. Two suspects were charged in connection with the arson attack on a cultural center in Altdöbern, Brandenburg (October 2025); two others were accused of attempted arson at an asylum seekers' home in Schmölln, Thuringia (January 2026). The Bundeskriminalamt (BKA) coordinated the operation with state security agencies. Federal prosecutors stated the suspects held extremist anti-immigration ideology and communicated via encrypted channels. The arrests underscored the BfV Verfassungsschutz's repeated warnings that far-right extremism — not Islamist terrorism — remains Germany's most dangerous domestic security threat.

media.caption: German police arrest five teenagers across 13 property raids for far-right 'Last Defense Wave' terror network

title: Wadephul at NATO Helsingborg Ministerial — Germany Proposes Ukraine Multilateral Financing Mechanism
detail: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul traveled to Helsingborg, Sweden for the NATO Foreign Ministers meeting (May 21-22) to prepare for the July NATO Summit in Ankara. At the meeting, Wadephul formally proposed a new multilateral NATO financing mechanism to address the approximately €40B gap in Ukraine's 2026 financing needs remaining after the EU's €90B loan facility was established. The mechanism would allow NATO allies to pool Ukraine support contributions independently of the US security umbrella — reflecting Germany's broader push for European strategic autonomy. Wadephul also confirmed Germany as one of the first NATO members to formally commit to the 5% of GDP defense spending target championed by the Trump administration. Germany's 2026 defense budget stands at approximately €108B (about 2.3% GDP), with a stated target of reaching 3.5% by 2029 through the Sondervermögen special fund and structural budget increases.

media.caption: FM Wadephul at NATO Helsingborg ministerial proposes multilateral Ukraine financing mechanism
